idiom_name: Room @Embedded(prefix) for Android, JPA @Embeddable/@Embedded on the server
implementation_notes: Kotlin's data classes already give the value semantics the pattern wants (equals/hashCode/copy from the primary constructor), and the mapping itself is supplied by the surrounding framework: on Android, Room's @Embedded annotation makes the sub-fields columns of the entity's own table, with an optional prefix so a value used twice does not collide - and Room notes that a @PrimaryKey inside an embedded type does not become the owner's key, which is exactly the no-identity rule. On the server the same decision is expressed with JPA's @Embeddable/@Embedded pair. The classic mapper class is never written; what remains is choosing the prefix and keeping the value immutable.
pitfalls: Room's prefix is always applied, even to a sub-field that has its own @ColumnInfo(name = ...), so the effective column name is prefix + name and not the name you wrote.

Room only reconstructs the embedded value when at least one of its columns is non-NULL; if every column is NULL the property is set to null, so a non-nullable Kotlin type with all-nullable columns will fail at runtime.
Two occurrences of the same embedded type without distinct prefixes map to the same columns - Room reports a duplicate column error only at compile time of the DAO, not of the entity.
